summaryZh: CNH Industrial最新调查显示，71%的北美农民将精准技术视为运营核心，超半数计划未来两年增加投资。自动驾驶、AI等前沿技术已在14%的受访农场落地。农民采用技术的主要动机是降低投入成本（74%）和节省时间（70%），而成本（56%）仍是最大 adoption 障碍。文章揭示了精准农业从基础导航到AI自动化的演进路径及市场渗透现状。
featuredReason: 该调查数据为智慧畜牧领域的设备商和服务商提供了北美市场精准技术渗透率、采纳动机与障碍的一手参考，有助于判断技术推广策略和产品定价方向。

Survey: Farmers double down on technology

CNH reveals 71% of North American farmers consider precision technology essential to operations.

Andy Castillo,Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery,Farm ProgressAugust 20, 2026

schedule2 Min Read

Precision agriculture technology guides tractors through mapped fields, reducing input costs while increasing yields. Thomas Barwick/Getty Images

The notion that farmers are behind the times is itself antiquated. A new report from CNH Industrial found that 71% of 217 North American farmers and ranchers surveyed consider technology an integral part of their operations, and more than half expect to increase their investments over the next two years.

“The next chapter of precision agriculture will be defined by making technology easier to use, easier to trust and easier to prove its value,” said Eric Shuman, head of global product management at CNH Industrial.

That’s a charge all modern machinery manufacturers are taking seriously. Over the last several decades, farm technology has advanced in leaps and bounds. Today’s autonomous and swath technology is built on yesterday’s innovation. Self-driving machines wouldn’t be possible without autosteer, just like drones couldn’t fly guess rows without field mapping.

Those foundational technologies are widely adopted, according to the study. Nearly 9 in 10 farmers operating CNH equipment use autoguidance, including GPS, autosteer and mapping. Of those surveyed, 54% use precision application systems such as adjustable fertilizer and spraying. The same percentage rely on telematics and integrated farm management platforms to collect and leverage data.

Related:How to pick and choose farm tech in the age of ‘decision’ ag

With that technological foundation built, cutting-edge technology is beginning to make its way onto American farms. Artificial intelligence and automation are being used on 14% of farms surveyed.

A strong yes

The impact can be felt beyond convenience. Of the respondents, 62% said their precision tech was moderately or extremely useful, increasing to 70% among cash crop producers. Here’s why farmers are adopting more technology:

74% to reduce input costs

70% to save time and improve labor efficiency

59% for increased yields

56% to conserve fuel

49% to collect better operational data

Taking a pass

But while the benefits seem enticing, there are barriers to adoption. The respondents gave these reasons for not buying:

56% for cost

36% for value

21% for needed training

As technology progresses, the price will come down. It’s a safe bet that cutting-edge technologies like automation will be as necessary to future farmers as autosteer is to today’s growers.

About the Author

Andy Castillo

Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery, Farm Progress

Andy Castillo started his career in journalism about a decade ago as a television news cameraperson and producer before transitioning to a regional newspaper covering western Massachusetts, where he wrote about local farming. Between military deployments with the Air Force and covering the news, he earned an MFA in creative nonfiction writing from Bay Path University, building on the English degree he earned from the University of Massachusetts Amherst. In his role at Farm Progress, Castillo covers agricultural technology, new machinery and the constantly evolving farm equipment marketplace.

Castillo splits his time between the open road and western Massachusetts with his wife, Brianna, a travel nurse who specializes in pediatric oncology, and their rescue pup, Rio. When not attending farm shows, Castillo enjoys playing music, snowboarding, writing, cooking and restoring their 1920 craftsman bungalow. You can find Castillo at farm machinery shows across the country.

translationZh:
农民落伍的观念本身已经过时。CNH Industrial的一份新报告发现，在接受调查的217名北美农民和牧场主中，71%的人认为技术是其运营中不可或缺的一部分，超过半数的人预计在未来两年内将增加相关投资。

“精准农业的下一个篇章将致力于让技术更易于使用、更易于信任、更易于证明其价值，”CNH Industrial全球产品管理主管Eric Shuman表示。

这是所有现代机械制造商都在认真对待的一项使命。在过去几十年里，农业技术取得了飞跃式发展。今天的自主和幅宽控制技术建立在昨日的创新之上。没有自动转向，就不可能有自动驾驶机械，就像没有田间测绘，无人机就无法在“猜测行”中飞行一样。

根据这项研究，这些基础技术已被广泛采用。近十分之九操作CNH设备的农民使用自动导航，包括GPS、自动转向和测绘。在接受调查的人中，54%使用精准施用系统，如可调节施肥和喷洒。同样比例的人依赖远程信息处理和集成农场管理平台来收集和利用数据。

相关：在“决策”农业时代如何挑选农场技术

在这一技术基础之上，前沿技术开始进入美国农场。在接受调查的农场中，人工智能和自动化已在14%的农场上得到应用。

**明确的肯定**

其影响不仅仅体现在便利性上。62%的受访者表示，他们的精准技术具有中等或极高实用性，而在经济作物生产者中，这一比例上升到70%。以下是农民更多采用技术的原因：

74%为了降低投入成本

70%为了节省时间和提高劳动效率

59%为了提高产量

56%为了节约燃料

49%为了收集更好的运营数据

**选择放弃**

但是，尽管好处似乎很诱人，但采用仍存在障碍。受访者给出了不购买的原因：

56%因为成本

36%因为价值

21%因为需要培训

随着技术的进步，价格将会下降。可以肯定的是，像自动化这样的前沿技术对于未来的农民来说，将像今天的自动转向对于种植者一样不可或缺。
